label: Site report
description: Field / site / incident report: a generated, dated, referenced page with a summary or progress note, a next-step line, a capture time and GPS for the photo, and contractor / client signature blocks. Anchored on the customer's site-report photo (demo/review/review.jpeg, OCR'd with jdf-cli 0.2.3 + tesseract on 2026-09-28: 'PROJECT REPORT GENERATED - 8 JULY 2026', 'REPORT ID + RPT-260708-E7BE23', 'SUMMARY / PROGRESS — Vehicle sustained ...', 'NEXT Request an inspection ...', 'CAPTURED - 8 JUL 2026 - 0:44 GMT+10 - GPS - -27.55344, 152.88712 - EXIF VERIFIED', 'CONTRACTOR CLIENT / Signature & Date'). Without this schema the page stayed uncertain and every claim about it was a manufactured 'field not found'.
notes: 2026-09-28: keywords are the report's own furniture (project/site/progress/inspection/incident report, captured, gps, exif, report id, scan to verify, signature & date); generic words (summary, next, client alone) were kept out of the family cues so a policy's 'summary of coverage' does not pull it here. The middle-dot separators of designed reports ('REPORT ID · RPT-…') reach these anchors through the raw-candidate projection (services/raw_candidates): tesseract read the dot as '+' and '-' on the customer's photo, and the label pass alone read '+ RPT-…' as debris.
